- When sentiment is negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 10-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.33 for 3+ consecutive days), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 2–5% to prevent overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 70–75), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.
- For 30d forecasts, if history shows high volatility (std > 2.5) and sentiment is mixed, use 14-day EWMA to dampen noise and avoid overfitting to recent extremes.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.2 or lower for 3+ days), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
